items.stem: A clock tower restoration crew starts with a full supply of gold leaf. It uses 3/5 of the supply in the first week and 1/4 of the original supply in the second week. What fraction of the original supply is left?
items.explanation: Add the two amounts used: 3/5 + 1/4 = 12/20 + 5/20 = 17/20. Then 1 - 17/20 = 3/20 remains. Choosing 17/20 reports the amount used instead of the amount left. Choosing 7/20 subtracts the second week from the first week. Choosing 1/3 invents a share by treating the two weeks as parts of a different whole.

items.stem: A night-sky star party sold 64 tickets last autumn and 88 tickets this autumn. By what percent did ticket sales increase?
items.explanation: The change is 88 - 64 = 24 tickets, and 24 / 64 = 0.375, which is 37.5%. Choosing 27.3% divides the change by the new total, 88, instead of the original, 64. Choosing 24% reports the raw change in tickets as if it were a percent. Choosing 3.75% slips the decimal point when converting 0.375 to a percent.

items.stem: A glassware shop displays 156 pieces: goblets, tumblers and vases in the ratio 5 to 4 to 3. How many more goblets than vases are on display?
items.explanation: The ratio parts total 5 + 4 + 3 = 12, so each part is 156 / 12 = 13 pieces. Goblets are 5 x 13 = 65 and vases are 3 x 13 = 39, a difference of 26. Choosing 13 stops at the size of one part. Choosing 39 gives the number of vases alone. Choosing 52 gives the number of tumblers, the middle group.

items.stem: A kayak on a calm, wide lagoon drifts steadily at 1.8 meters per second, pushed only by the current. How many meters does it drift in 25 minutes?
items.explanation: Twenty-five minutes is 25 x 60 = 1,500 seconds, and 1,500 x 1.8 = 2,700 meters. Choosing 45 multiplies the speed by 25 without changing minutes to seconds. Choosing 108 gives the distance for only one minute. Choosing 1,500 converts the time to seconds but never multiplies by the speed.

items.stem: A local radio call-in desk logged 14 calls in 35 minutes. At the same steady pace, how many calls will it log in 2 1/2 hours?
items.explanation: The pace is 14 / 35 = 0.4 calls per minute, and 2 1/2 hours is 150 minutes, so the desk logs 0.4 x 150 = 60 calls. Choosing 150 reads the number of minutes as the number of calls. Choosing 375 uses 2.5 minutes per call instead of the rate. Choosing 2,100 multiplies 14 by 150 and ignores the 35 minutes.

items.stem: A thrift fabric shop sells wool at $4.08 per yard. Which is the best estimate of the cost of 29 yards?
items.explanation: Round 29 yards to 30 and $4.08 to $4, so the estimate is 30 x 4 = $120, close to the exact $118.32. Choosing $90 rounds the price down to $3. Choosing $150 rounds the price up to $5. Choosing $1,200 slips a decimal place and treats the price as $40 per yard.

items.stem: A school robotics pit crew writes 3(2x + 1) - 5 = x + 28 to decide how many spare drive chains, x, to pack. What is the value of x?
items.explanation: Distribute to get 6x + 3 - 5 = x + 28, so 6x - 2 = x + 28. Subtract x and add 2: 5x = 30, so x = 6. Choosing 6.4 forgets to multiply the 1 by 3. Choosing 4 treats the -5 as +5. Choosing 30 stops at 5x = 30 and never divides by 5.

items.stem: A rowing regatta office has $500 to spend on trophies. Each trophy costs $23, and a one-time engraving fee is $65. What is the greatest number of trophies the office can buy?
items.explanation: The inequality is 23t + 65 <= 500, so 23t <= 435 and t <= 18.9. Only whole trophies can be bought, so the greatest number is 18. Choosing 19 rounds 18.9 up, which would cost more than $500. Choosing 21 divides 500 by 23 and forgets the engraving fee. Choosing 435 stops after subtracting the fee.

items.stem: During a star party, the temperature was 61 degrees at 9 p.m. and fell at a steady rate to 45 degrees at 1 a.m. Which equation gives the temperature T, in degrees, t hours after 9 p.m.?
items.explanation: The temperature changed by 45 - 61 = -16 degrees over 4 hours, a slope of -4 degrees per hour. At t = 0 the temperature is 61, so T = -4t + 61. Choosing -16t uses the total drop as the rate. Choosing +45 uses the final temperature as the starting value. Choosing 4t gives a rising temperature.

items.stem: A town band’s uniform fund follows the formula C = 45n + 120, where C is the cost in dollars and n is the number of members fitted. Which equation solves the formula for n?
items.explanation: Subtract 120 from both sides to get C - 120 = 45n, then divide the whole left side by 45, so n = (C - 120) / 45. Choosing the first wrong form divides only the 120 and leaves C alone. Choosing +120 adds when it should subtract. Choosing 45(C - 120) multiplies instead of dividing by the coefficient.

items.stem: A glassware shop sells small vases and large vases. Four small vases and three large vases cost $78 together, and two small vases and five large vases cost $88 together. What is the price of one large vase?
items.explanation: Double the second equation to get 4s + 10l = 176, then subtract 4s + 3l = 78 to get 7l = 98, so l = 14, and s = 9 follows. Choosing $9 gives the small vase price instead. Choosing $23 adds the two prices. Choosing $98 stops at 7l = 98 and never divides by 7.

items.stem: A clock tower workshop cuts a rectangular brass plate whose area is 3x^2 + 10x - 8 square inches. Which pair of expressions gives the length and the width?
items.explanation: Multiply 3x by x for 3x^2 and -2 by 4 for -8. The cross terms 12x and -2x add to 10x, so (3x - 2)(x + 4) works. The pair (3x + 2)(x - 4) gives -10x. The pair (3x - 4)(x + 2) gives +2x. The pair (3x + 4)(x - 2) gives -2x. Each wrong pair has the right end terms but the wrong middle term.

items.stem: A kayak rental pier models its daily profit, in hundreds of dollars, as P(x) = -2x^2 + 16x - 30, where x is the hourly rental price in dollars. At which price x is the profit greatest?
items.explanation: The graph opens downward, so the greatest value is at the vertex, where x = -b / (2a) = -16 / (2 x -2) = 4. Choosing $8 divides 16 by 2 and drops the negative sign of a. Choosing $16 reads the coefficient of x as the price. Choosing $2 reports the greatest profit, P(4) = 2, instead of the price that produces it.

items.stem: Two arms of a kayak storage rack meet a straight wall rail, forming supplementary angles that measure (3x + 10) degrees and (5x - 6) degrees. What is the value of x?
items.explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180, so 3x + 10 + 5x - 6 = 180, which gives 8x + 4 = 180 and 8x = 176, so x = 22. Choosing 176 stops at 8x = 176 and never divides by 8. Choosing 76 gives the measure of the first angle, 3(22) + 10, not x. Choosing 104 gives the second angle, 5(22) - 6.

items.stem: A kayak storage tray is a triangular prism. Its triangular end has a base of 7 inches and a height of 12 inches, and the tray is 11 inches long. What is its volume?
options: 42 cubic inches
77 cubic inches
462 cubic inches
924 cubic inches
items.explanation: The triangle’s area is 1/2 x 7 x 12 = 42 square inches, and multiplying by the 11-inch length gives 462 cubic inches. Choosing 924 forgets the one-half. Choosing 42 stops at the area of the end. Choosing 77 multiplies only the base and the length, which ignores the height.

items.stem: A clock tower casts a shadow 18 meters long. At the same moment, a 1.5-meter marker post casts a shadow 0.9 meter long. How tall is the clock tower?
options: 10.8 meters
16.2 meters
27 meters
30 meters
items.explanation: Similar triangles give height / 18 = 1.5 / 0.9, so the tower is 18 x 1.5 / 0.9 = 30 meters tall. Choosing 10.8 flips the proportion and computes 0.9 x 18 / 1.5. Choosing 16.2 multiplies 18 by 0.9 and never uses the post height. Choosing 27 multiplies 18 by 1.5 and never divides by 0.9.

items.stem: A night-sky star party volunteer picks one eyepiece case at random from a shelf holding 10 plossl cases, 8 wide-field cases and 6 zoom cases. What is the probability that the case is a plossl or a zoom case?
items.explanation: There are 10 + 8 + 6 = 24 cases, and 10 + 6 = 16 of them are plossl or zoom, so the probability is 16/24 = 2/3. Choosing 5/12 counts only the plossl cases. Choosing 1/3 gives the wide-field cases, the outcome that is left out. Choosing 7/12 counts the wide-field and zoom cases instead.

items.stem: Six rowers’ practice distances, in kilometers, have a mean of 15.5. Five of the distances are 18, 16, 15, 17 and 19. What is the sixth distance?
options: 8 km
17 km
93 km
items.explanation: The six distances must total 6 x 15.5 = 93, and the five known ones total 85, so the sixth is 93 - 85 = 8. Choosing 93 stops at the total. Choosing 17 gives the mean of the five known distances. Choosing 15.5 assumes the missing value equals the overall mean.

items.stem: A thrift fabric shop sold the following yards of cloth on eight days: 14, 9, 22, 17, 9, 31, 12 and 20. What is the median number of yards sold?
items.explanation: Order the values: 9, 9, 12, 14, 17, 20, 22, 31. With eight values, the median is the mean of the fourth and fifth values, (14 + 17) / 2 = 15.5. Choosing 14 takes only the fourth value. Choosing 12 picks the third value. Choosing 9 reports the mode, the value that appears twice.

items.stem: A kayak rental pier surveyed 80 renters, and 28 of them rented a tandem kayak. If the same rate holds, about how many of the next 1,200 renters will rent a tandem kayak?
items.explanation: The rate is 28 / 80 = 0.35, and 0.35 x 1,200 = 420 renters. Choosing 15 divides 1,200 by 80 and never uses the 28. Choosing 4,200 multiplies 1,200 by 28 / 8, slipping a decimal place in the rate. Choosing 780 predicts the renters who will not choose a tandem kayak, the other part of the whole.

items.stem:
The wooden sign over the pier said Salt Hollow Rentals, though nobody had paid rent there in years. Marguerite unlocked the shed, flipped the damp life jackets onto the rail, and counted the paddles twice, as her father always had. Eleven. There had never been eleven; he insisted on twelve, an even dozen, like eggs. She lined the paddles up anyway, blade to blade, and left a gap at the end of the rack, just wide enough for one more. Then she propped the door open to the morning and waited for the first customers.

Which idea does the gap Marguerite leaves in the paddle rack most strongly suggest?
options: She plans to buy a new paddle that morning.
She is careless about how the paddles are stored.
She hopes customers will not notice the missing paddle.
She is keeping a place for something her father valued.
items.explanation: The detail that her father insisted on twelve, an even dozen, and that she counted twice as he always had, shows she is honoring his habit. Leaving a gap just wide enough for one more keeps his missing paddle’s place. Buying a paddle is never mentioned. Carelessness contradicts her careful lining up. Hiding the shortage from customers does not fit, since she leaves the gap in plain view.

items.stem:
The uniform closet behind the band room smelled of cedar and old brass polish. Dev ran his thumb along the shoulder seam of a red jacket that had been worn by thirty years of trombonists, each one slightly broader or narrower than the last. The wool had gone soft at the elbows and stiff at the collar. When he slid his arms in, the sleeves stopped an inch short of his wrists, but the buttons closed, and in the mirror he looked, for the first time all fall, like someone who belonged to the row.

What does the word “stiff” most nearly mean as it is used in the passage?
options: formal and unfriendly in manner
resistant to bending from age and wear
painful and sore after exercise
unusually strong and durable
items.explanation: The sentence contrasts the elbows, which have gone soft with use, with the collar, which has gone stiff, so the word describes fabric that no longer bends easily. The meaning formal and unfriendly describes a person’s manner, but the jacket is a piece of cloth. Painful and sore describes a body, which does not fit wool. Unusually strong ignores that the wool is worn, not new.

items.stem:
Odalys had worked the regatta office for six summers, and she knew its sounds: the stapler’s sharp bite, the radio muttering wind speeds, the bell on the door that never rang gently. So when the door opened without any bell at all, she looked up from the heat sheets expecting a draft. Instead a girl of about nine stood on the mat holding a trophy as tall as her arm. “It’s the wrong name,” the girl whispered. “Somebody spelled me wrong.” Odalys set down her pen and, for the first time that week, found she was in no hurry.

What is the main purpose of the first sentence of the passage?
options: It establishes the office as a familiar place where Odalys is used to its routines.
It explains exactly why the girl came to the office carrying such a large trophy.
It shows that Odalys is bored with her job and plans to leave the regatta office soon.
It introduces a conflict between Odalys and the coworkers who share her office.
items.explanation: The opening sentence and the list of sounds show that Odalys knows the office well, and that familiarity makes the silent door and the girl’s arrival stand out. The girl’s reason appears later, in her own words. Nothing says Odalys is bored or wants to leave. No coworkers appear at all, so no conflict with them is set up.

items.stem:
The thrift shop’s fabric room was one long, crowded aisle, and Wen had spent the afternoon sorting remnants by color. Near the back she found a bolt of blue cotton, faded along its fold into the pale shade of morning sky. She unrolled a yard of it and held it to the window. The flaw she had noticed, a thin wandering line where the dye had skipped, now caught the light like a river on a map. She almost marked it down as damaged. Instead she wrote, in careful marker, “Sold by the yard, river included.”

Which statement best expresses a theme of the passage?
options: Careful sorting always leads to profit for a shop that keeps its shelves neat.
Faded things should be replaced with new ones as soon as a flaw appears.
An apparent flaw can be seen as a feature worth keeping.
Shop work is more rewarding than most other jobs a person could take.
items.explanation: Wen first sees the skipped dye as a flaw, then compares it to a river on a map, and finally advertises it as part of the cloth. That sequence shows a flaw being reframed as a feature. The passage never connects sorting to profit, never recommends replacing faded things, and never compares shop work with any other kind of job.

items.stem:
Glass that cools too quickly can look perfect and still fail weeks later. When a glassblower finishes a piece, the outside surface cools faster than the core, and the two layers shrink at different rates. The result is hidden stress. To prevent it, shops place finished work in an oven called an annealer, which holds the glass at a high temperature and then lowers it slowly over many hours. A thin goblet may need only a few hours, while a thick paperweight can need several days. Skipping this step is a common reason that new glassware cracks without being touched.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Thin glassware is stronger than thick glassware because it cools in less time.
Glassblowers should avoid using an annealer for small pieces because they cool fast.
Glass that looks flawless never fails after it is finished and cooled completely.
Slow, controlled cooling protects glassware from hidden stress that can make it crack.
items.explanation: The passage explains why uneven cooling creates hidden stress and how an annealer’s slow cooling prevents later cracking, which is the main idea. It never says thin glass is stronger; it says thin pieces need less time. It recommends the annealer, not avoiding it. The opening sentence says the opposite of the last choice.

items.stem:
Kayak hulls are shaped for specific jobs. A long, narrow hull cuts through water with little resistance, so it glides farther with each stroke, but it can feel tippy to a beginner. A short, wide hull turns quickly and feels stable, though it takes more effort to move in a straight line. Rental piers that serve first-time paddlers therefore stock mostly wide hulls, while touring clubs favor the narrow kind. Hull length and width are listed in every manufacturer’s specifications, so a buyer can compare designs before ever touching the water.

According to the passage, why do rental piers for first-time paddlers stock mostly wide hulls?
options: Wide hulls glide farther with each stroke.
Wide hulls cost less than narrow hulls.
Wide hulls feel stable to beginners.
Wide hulls are favored by touring clubs.
items.explanation: The passage states that a short, wide hull feels stable, and that rental piers serving first-time paddlers stock mostly wide hulls for that reason. Gliding farther is a feature of the long, narrow hull. Cost is never discussed. Touring clubs are said to favor the narrow kind, which reverses the last choice.

items.stem:
When a caller reaches a local radio show, the voice on the air is only the last step. First, a screener answers the line and asks what the caller wants to say. The screener types a one-line summary into the host’s screen and flags callers who are off topic, confused or unwilling to wait. Some shows also use a delay of a few seconds so that an unexpected remark can be cut before it airs. These small steps do not make the conversation less spontaneous; they let the host spend the broadcast listening instead of untangling problems.

Based on the passage, what is the role of a screener?
options: To help the host by sorting calls before they reach the air.
To decide the topic of the show each day.
To cut every call after a few seconds.
To prevent callers from saying anything unplanned.
items.explanation: The passage says the screener asks what the caller wants, types a summary and flags problem calls, so the host can listen rather than untangle problems. That supports the claim that screeners sort calls. Choosing the show’s topic is never mentioned. The delay applies to remarks, not to all calls. The passage says the steps do not make the conversation less spontaneous.

items.stem:
Wool, cotton and polyester behave very differently in a washing machine, which is why a thrift fabric shop keeps them on separate racks. Wool fibers have tiny scales that lock together when heated and agitated, so a sweater can shrink by a full size in one wash. Cotton shrinks mainly the first time it meets hot water. Polyester barely shrinks at all, but it can hold odors that the fiber traps. A buyer who checks the label for fiber content before buying a remnant can avoid unwelcome surprises at home.

How does the author organize the information in the passage?
options: By telling a story about one customer’s shopping trip through the fabric shop’s aisles
By comparing how three fibers react to washing and ending with practical advice
By listing the history of each fiber in order from the oldest to the newest
By arguing that one fiber is clearly better than the other two for every buyer
items.explanation: The passage takes each of the three fibers in turn, explains how it reacts to washing, and closes with advice about checking labels. That is a comparison followed by a practical recommendation. There is no customer story, no historical sequence, and no argument that a single fiber is best, since each fiber’s drawback is noted as well.

items.stem:
A school robotics pit crew has only a few minutes between matches to repair a robot, so the team practices as carefully as it builds. Each member holds one job, such as battery swaps, bumper checks or software resets, and rehearses it until the motions are automatic. Teams often time these drills and post the results on a wall. The goal is not speed alone. A crew that rushes may forget a loose bolt, so coaches count accuracy first and treat the clock as a second measure.

What is the author’s primary purpose in the passage?
options: To persuade readers to join a robotics team
To criticize teams that time their drills
To describe the history of robotics competitions
To explain how pit crews prepare for fast repairs
items.explanation: The passage describes the roles, rehearsals and priorities that pit crews use, so its purpose is to explain how they prepare. It never urges readers to join. It does not criticize timing, since timed drills are described as normal, with accuracy counted first. Nothing in it covers the history of competitions.

items.stem:
On a clear, moonless night, a person far from city lights can see thousands of stars. In a town with bright streetlamps, that number can drop to a few dozen. Astronomers call this glow light pollution, and it is caused mainly by light that shines upward or sideways instead of down toward the ground. Shielded fixtures solve much of the problem by pointing light only where it is needed. Some towns have also switched to warmer-colored bulbs, which scatter less in the atmosphere. Such changes help stargazers, but they also save energy.

What does the word “scatter” most nearly mean as it is used in the passage?
options: fall to the ground
spread in many directions
burn out quickly
gather in one place
items.explanation: The passage says warmer bulbs scatter less in the atmosphere, in the context of light that glows upward and sideways and brightens the sky. In that setting, scatter means to spread light in many directions. Falling to the ground is what shielded fixtures aim for. Burning out quickly is about bulb life, which is not discussed. Gathering in one place is the opposite meaning.

items.stem:
NOTICE: Saturday Foraging Walk. Meet at the north gate at 8:00 a.m. The two-hour walk covers wild blackberries, wild mint and rose hips only; no mushrooms will be gathered. Guides will teach participants to confirm each plant by leaf shape, stem and smell before picking. Please wear closed shoes and long sleeves, since brambles are thick along the creek. Bring a small container, but leave the sharp tools at home, because guides will carry shears for any cutting. Take only what you will eat that day, and leave at least two-thirds of each patch for birds and other walkers.

According to the notice, why should participants leave sharp tools at home?
options: Brambles along the creek are too thick to cut.
The walk covers only plants that need no cutting.
Guides will carry shears for any cutting.
Closed shoes make carrying tools unsafe.
items.explanation: The notice says to leave sharp tools at home because guides will carry shears for any cutting. It mentions thick brambles only as the reason for long sleeves and closed shoes. It does not say the plants need no cutting; it mentions cutting by the guides. Shoes are mentioned for protection and are never linked to tools.

items.stem:
Rowing regattas score races by finishing order, but the starting lanes are not chosen at random. In a typical regatta, crews first row a short time trial. The fastest crews are placed in the middle lanes, where the course is most sheltered from wind and current, and slower crews take the outer lanes. This arrangement keeps the strongest crews from being blown off line and makes close finishes easier to judge. Officials say the system rewards preparation, since a crew that trains well earns a calmer lane before the real race even begins.

Which detail from the passage best supports the claim that lane assignment rewards preparation?
options: The fastest crews in the time trial receive the more sheltered middle lanes.
Regattas score races by finishing order, as the first sentence of the passage states.
Slower crews take the outer lanes, where the wind and current are strongest.
Officials say close finishes are easier to judge when strong crews stay on line.
items.explanation: The detail that the fastest crews in the time trial are given the sheltered middle lanes directly links earlier performance to a better position. Scoring by finishing order does not mention preparation. The outer lanes for slower crews describe the opposite group and give no reward. Easier judging of finishes is a benefit to officials, not to crews.

items.stem:
A band uniform closet does more than store jackets. Wool is a favorite food of clothes moths, so each jacket is hung on a wide wooden hanger with a cedar block in its pocket, and the block is sanded lightly every autumn to renew its scent. Jackets hang a hand’s width apart so that air can circulate, since trapped dampness leads to mildew. Before storage each spring, a volunteer brushes every jacket and checks the seams. Closets kept this way can protect a uniform for decades, even when dozens of students wear it in turn.

Based on the passage, which conclusion about the care of band uniforms is best supported?
options: Moths are no longer a danger to wool jackets.
Cedar blocks make brushing the jackets unnecessary.
Uniforms should be washed each time a student wears them.
Regular, simple routines can protect wool uniforms for many years.
items.explanation: The passage describes several simple routines, such as cedar blocks, spacing, brushing and seam checks, and says they can protect a uniform for decades. Moths are named as a real danger that the routines guard against. Brushing is listed as a separate spring task. Washing after each wearing is never mentioned.

items.stem:
FIELD NOTES, clock tower, March 3. The pendulum swings once every two seconds, and the escapement gives a faint click at each swing. I counted 30 clicks in a minute, which matches the old maker’s plate. Today the clock ran four minutes slow. The keeper explained that a pendulum’s length sets its beat, and that metal rods expand slightly in warm air. A longer rod means a slower swing. He raised the small brass nut under the bob by a few turns, shortening the swing, and by evening the face agreed with my watch.

What does the passage suggest caused the clock to run slow?
options: The escapement had stopped clicking altogether.
The pendulum rod had grown longer in warm air.
The maker’s plate listed the wrong number of swings.
The keeper had loosened the nut the day before.
items.explanation: The keeper explains that metal rods expand in warm air and that a longer rod swings more slowly, then fixes the problem by shortening the swing. That points to a longer rod. The clicks were counted at 30 per minute, so the escapement still worked. The count matched the plate. Nothing says the keeper loosened the nut earlier.

items.stem:
Profile: Marisol Vega, the volunteer who runs the town’s night-sky star parties, never planned to become a teacher. She began by bringing a secondhand telescope to the park so her neighbors could see Saturn’s rings. People lined up, and she found she enjoyed answering their questions more than looking through the lens herself. Today she trains younger volunteers, each of whom learns to say “I don’t know, but let’s find out” before learning any constellation. She says that phrase keeps the nights friendly and the visitors curious.

Which word best describes the tone of the profile?
options: Admiring
Skeptical
Urgent
Humorous
items.explanation: The profile praises Marisol Vega’s generosity, her patience and her teaching philosophy, giving details that make her seem likable and effective, so the tone is admiring. Skeptical would require doubt about her work. Urgent would require pressure or a warning. Humorous would require jokes or playful exaggeration, and the passage has none.

items.stem: A glassblowing studio posted a short staff notice about the morning schedule. Which version of the notice uses the correct form of the verb?
options: Neither the apprentices nor the glassblower are ready when the oven opens.
The glassblower, along with two apprentices, are ready when the oven opens.
Neither the apprentices nor the glassblower is ready when the oven opens.
Each of the apprentices have a task when the oven opens.
items.explanation: When subjects are joined by neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, glassblower, which is singular, so is is correct. The version with are pairs a plural verb with that singular subject. The phrase along with two apprentices does not add to the subject, so are is wrong there too. The pronoun each is singular and needs has, not have.

items.stem: A regatta office posted a note about its opening hours and the first race. Which version of the sentence about the regatta office is punctuated correctly?
options: The regatta office opens at six; however, the first race does not start until eight.
The regatta office opens at six, however, the first race does not start until eight.
The regatta office opens at six however, the first race does not start until eight.
The regatta office opens at six; however the first race, does not start until eight.
items.explanation: A conjunctive adverb such as however joins two complete sentences, so it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it. The version with a comma before however creates a comma splice. The version with no mark before however runs the clauses together. The version that puts a comma after race splits the subject from its verb.

items.stem: “Walking along the pier at dawn, the kayaks looked like sleeping seals.” Which revision corrects the dangling modifier in this sentence?
options: Walking along the pier at dawn, the kayaks looked to Lena like sleeping seals.
The kayaks, walking along the pier at dawn, looked like sleeping seals.
Walking along the pier at dawn, the kayaks that looked like sleeping seals were seen.
Walking along the pier at dawn, Lena thought the kayaks looked like sleeping seals.
items.explanation: The opening phrase Walking along the pier must describe a person, so the sentence needs a person right after the comma, as in Lena thought. In the original, kayaks seem to be walking. The version that puts looked to Lena after kayaks still leaves the kayaks as the nearest subject. Moving the phrase beside kayaks makes the error clearer. The passive version keeps the kayaks as the doer.

items.stem: A thrift fabric shop manager lists what her new hires will do: “New hires will measure remnants, sort buttons by size, and ______” Which choice completes the sentence so that it is parallel?
options: labeling the shelves.
the shelves need labels.
label the shelves.
will be labeling shelves.
items.explanation: The list uses verbs in the same base form: measure remnants, sort buttons, and label the shelves. The form labeling the shelves shifts to an -ing verb. The clause the shelves need labels adds a new subject. The phrase will be labeling repeats the helping verb and changes the pattern. Parallel structure keeps every item in the same grammatical form.

items.stem: “The crew hoped the lighter paint would not ______ the clock tower’s weathered look.” Which choice correctly completes the sentence?
options: effect
affect
affected by
effecting
items.explanation: The sentence needs a verb meaning to influence, and affect is the verb that fits after the helping word would not. Effect is usually a noun meaning a result, though it can mean to bring about. The phrase affected by is a participle phrase that cannot follow would not. Effecting would need a helping verb and does not mean influence.

items.stem: “Dara told Wen that she had left the radio schedule on the studio desk.” Which revision best corrects the unclear pronoun in this sentence?
options: Dara told Wen that she, herself, had left the radio schedule on the studio desk.
Dara told Wen that she had left it on the studio desk.
Dara told Wen, “I left the radio schedule on the studio desk.”
Dara told Wen that she had left the radio schedule there.
items.explanation: In the original, she could mean either Dara or Wen. Quoting Dara’s own words removes the confusion, because the first-person pronoun I can refer only to the speaker. Adding herself still leaves doubt about who is meant. Replacing the schedule with it adds a second vague pronoun. Replacing the desk with there changes the location but keeps the unclear she.

items.stem: A town newsletter describes the glassware shop and the workshop it runs for young visitors. Which sentence uses the possessive form correctly?
options: The glassware shops’ two ovens heat the childrens’ workshop upstairs.
The glassware shop’s two ovens heat the children’s workshop upstairs.
The glassware shop’s two ovens heat the childrens workshop upstairs.
The glassware shops two ovens heat the children’s workshop upstairs.
items.explanation: A single shop takes an apostrophe before the s, shop’s, and children is already plural, so the possessive is children’s. The form shops’ would mean more than one shop. The form childrens’ puts the apostrophe after an irregular plural that does not end in s. The form childrens leaves out the apostrophe entirely. The form shops with no apostrophe fails to show ownership.

items.stem: “Last summer the radio desk hosted a weekly show, and listeners call in with questions.” Which revision makes the verb tenses in this sentence consistent?
options: Last summer the radio desk hosted a weekly show, and listeners called in with questions.
Last summer the radio desk hosts a weekly show, and listeners called in with questions.
Last summer the radio desk hosted a weekly show, and listeners will call in with questions.
Last summer the radio desk hosted a weekly show, and listeners are calling in with questions.
items.explanation: Last summer places both actions in the past, so the second verb must be the past form called, matching hosted. Changing the first verb to hosts puts the sentence in a mixed tense. Will call moves the second action into the future. Are calling makes it a present action. Each of those leaves the two verbs out of step with each other.

items.stem: A school robotics team’s handbook gives short written rules for the pit crew before each match. Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: The pit crew checked: the battery, the bumpers and the wheels.
The pit crew checked one: thing before every match the battery.
The pit crew: checked one thing before every match, the battery.
The pit crew checked one thing before every match: the battery.
items.explanation: A colon may follow a complete sentence to introduce a word, phrase or list, and The pit crew checked one thing before every match is complete before the colon. The version with the colon right after the verb checked interrupts a clause. The colon inside the phrase one thing splits it. The colon after the subject crew separates it from its verb.

items.stem: “The star party drew ______ visitors than last year because clouds covered the sky.” Which choice completes the sentence correctly?
options: less
fewer
lesser
least
items.explanation: Visitors can be counted, so the comparison needs fewer. Less is used with amounts that cannot be counted, such as light or time. Lesser describes importance or rank, as in the lesser of two choices. Least is the superlative and does not fit a comparison with last year, which involves only two things.

items.stem: A restoration log from the clock tower contains this pair of sentences: “Because the fog covered the tower. The crew stopped work.” Which choice corrects the sentence fragment?
options: Because the fog covered the tower; the crew stopped work.
Because the fog covered the tower, and the crew stopped work.
Because the fog covered the tower, the crew stopped work.
Because the fog covered the tower. So the crew stopped work.
items.explanation: A clause beginning with because cannot stand alone, so it must be joined to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon requires a complete sentence on both sides. Adding and after the comma makes the because clause lack a main clause. Starting a sentence with So leaves the fragment in place.

items.stem:
(1) The kayak pier opens in May. (2) Rentals are busiest on weekends. (3) Staff arrive at seven to inspect every boat. (4) Visitors should reserve a boat early.

The writer wants sentence 4 to show a clear link to sentence 2. Which revision best accomplishes this?
options: Visitors should reserve a boat early, which is a good idea.
In addition, visitors should reserve a boat early.
Visitors should reserve a boat early, and the pier opens in May.
Because weekends fill quickly, visitors should reserve a boat early.
items.explanation: The revision begins with a reason taken from sentence 2, that weekends are busy, so the advice follows logically from the fact. The phrase which is a good idea adds no link. In addition suggests a separate point and not a cause. Repeating that the pier opens in May goes back to sentence 1 and breaks the focus on reserving.

items.stem: A paragraph about a glassware shop contains these two sentences: “The glassblower finished the vase. The vase was blue.” The writer wants to combine them with the next sentence, “She set it in the annealer.” Which choice combines all three most effectively?
options: After finishing the blue vase, the glassblower set it in the annealer.
The glassblower finished the vase, the vase was blue, she set it in the annealer.
The glassblower finished the vase and it was blue and she set it in the annealer.
Having finished, the blue vase was set in the annealer by the glassblower.
items.explanation: The best combination turns the second sentence into the adjective blue and the first into an opening phrase, leaving one clear subject and verb. The comma-only version is a run-on. The and version strings clauses together without emphasis. The last version starts with Having finished, which wrongly attaches to the vase and leaves the glassblower as a passive agent.

items.stem: A draft about the town clock reads: “At this point in time, the museum is currently in the process of restoring the old clock.” The writer wants to make the sentence clear and concise without changing its meaning. Which revision is best?
options: The museum is currently restoring the old clock at this time.
At present, the museum is in the process of restoring the clock.
The museum, right now, is presently working on restoring the old clock.
The museum is restoring the old clock.
items.explanation: The best revision removes the repeated time markers and the empty phrase in the process of, since is restoring already shows the work is ongoing. The version that keeps currently and at this time still repeats the idea of now. The version that keeps in the process of stays wordy. The last version repeats right now and presently and adds working on.

items.stem: A student’s paragraph about a thrift fabric shop reads: “The shop sorts remnants by color and weight. Volunteers press and fold every piece before it reaches the shelf. Buyers can find a small square of silk or a full bolt of denim in minutes.” Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
options: Fabric can be made from many different materials, including cotton, wool, silk and linen.
Some shoppers prefer to buy cloth online instead of visiting a crowded shop in person.
This careful sorting turns a crowded room of leftovers into a shop where shoppers find what they need quickly.
The shop is located in the center of town, a short walk from the old clock tower.
items.explanation: A concluding sentence should tie together the paragraph’s details, and the sentence about careful sorting connects the sorting, pressing and folding to the buyers’ quick search. The sentence about materials broadens the topic without linking to the sorting. The sentence about online shopping introduces a new point. The sentence about the shop’s location is unrelated to the process described.
